 Celtic flop joins unwanted former Rangers star at summit of unlikely Conference League top scorers’ list 
 David Robson 
 , Online Sports Reporter 
 Published:
 09:33, 23 Oct 2026 
 | 
 Updated:
 09:35, 23 Oct 2026 
 Add us as a preferred source

 CELTIC crashed to their third consecutive Europa League defeat against Celta Vigo as a quick-fire double from Javi Rodriguez silenced Parkhead.
 But while Martin O’Neill ‘s men plummeted down the Europa League table, a former Celtic flop was busy climbing to the summit of European football’s third tier.
 He netted a double in a shock European win Credit: Reuters 
 His side are two for two in the Conference League Credit: AP 
 Advertisement 
 Ex-Hoops striker Albian Ajeti has shot to the top of the Conference League scoring charts after netting a brace in a stunning victory over Spanish outfit Getafe — taking his tally to three goals in just two games.
 The Swiss striker levelled the match between Getafe and Lugano after just three minutes in Madrid following a crazy start, with Ivan Azon having fired the hosts ahead after just 71 seconds.

 Then in the seventh minute, Ajeti turned provider as he set up team-mate Yanis Cimignani to make it 2-1 in an incredible turn of events .
 Ajeti grabbed his second in the 26th minute as the Swiss league leaders started running riot, with the ex-Celtic striker right at the forefront.

 The match finished 5-2 in an astonishing scalp for Lugano, who continued their perfect start to their Conference League campaign with two wins out of two.
 They sit second in the table behind Greek side Panathinaikos, who are flying high at the top — thanks to a former Rangers frontman.
 Panathinaikos thrashed Celtic’s old foes Kairat Almaty 5-1 in Kazakhstan in their biggest European win for 49 years, dating back to a 4-0 victory over Floriana in 1977.
 And ex-Rangers striker Cyriel Dessers was the star of the show , netting a brace to fire his side to back-to-back Conference League wins.

 He scored Panathinaikos’ second from the penalty spot in the 24th minute after being fouled in the box, before making it 3-0 just two minutes into the second half with a powerful strike .
 That double takes him to three goals in two games in the competition , having also netted a penalty against Borac in the opening match.
 That mirrors Ajeti, who was also on target in Lugano’s 3-2 win over Red Star Belgrade last month.
 Advertisement 
 Both players are now tied at the top of the Conference League goalscoring charts, alongside three other players who also boast three strikes .
 The ex-Old Firm duo are battling it out at the summit with Brann pair Niklas Castro and Noah Holm, as well as Franculino Dju of Trabzonspor.
